title: Facet brief
description: The client's request, understood: what the video is, for whom, where it plays, how long it runs and what the viewer takes away. The producer writes it at intake to artifacts/brief.json and restates it to the operator. Every answer is marked stated, inferred or unknown in answer_status; nothing the operator did not say is presented as their wish. Pipelines that go from intake straight to the script (most footage-led ones, avatar and localization) record the production plan a proposal would otherwise give in metadata.

hook.description: A working hook: the opening that makes the viewer stay.

key_points.description: Concrete claims the video makes, not topics.

core_message.description: One sentence the viewer remembers tomorrow.

cta.description: Call to action: one specific thing the viewer does next.

tone.description: What it should feel like, in the operator's own words where they reveal intent.

style.description: Style direction: a style id (clean-professional, flat-motion-graphics, minimalist-diagram, premium-minimalist, anime-ghibli) or a description of the look wanted.

target_audience.description: Who watches and what they already know.

target_platform.description: Where the video plays. It sets the frame size and the length.

reference_material.description: Paths or URLs of everything supplied: footage, audio, images, a script, a brand kit, a website or product, a music track, reference videos.

pipeline.description: The production method chosen at intake (pipelines_list, pipeline_describe).

stance.description: The producer stance, following the video's main job; the pipeline gives a default.

brand.description: Brand material the video must respect.

logo.description: Path or URL of the logo.

guidelines.description: Path or URL of the brand guidelines, or a short summary of them.

constraints.description: Deadline, must-include, must-avoid, and whether paid steps are welcome.

paid_steps_welcome.description: Whether the operator accepts tools that charge their provider accounts. Leave it out and mark it unknown when they have not said.

answer_status.description: How each answer was obtained. Keys are the seven intake questions (purpose, audience, platform, tone, references, outcome, constraints) or a field of this record; values are stated (the operator said it), inferred (you assumed it, for example a platform default, and said so) or unknown (still open).

angle_options.description: Early angles, when the operator wants to choose a direction before research. The proposal's concepts replace them.

selected_angle.description: The name of the angle the operator chose.

metadata.description: Free-form notes. Pipelines without research and proposal stages record here the plan a proposal would otherwise give, under production_plan, paid_steps and approval. Present that plan, stop, and record the operator's answer in approval. Other keys are allowed.

paid_steps.description: Every step that calls a paid tool; empty when the plan uses none.

plan.description: The production plan for a pipeline without a proposal stage. Same field names as production_plan in proposal_packet; the edit and compose stages read the locked settings from here.

treatment_options.description: Two or three treatments when the material can go different ways, with your recommendation marked.

description.description: What the video becomes with this treatment, and what it uses from the material.

selected_treatment.description: Id of the treatment the operator chose.

outputs.description: The deliverables: how many, frame sizes, durations, platforms, languages.

style.description: A style id, or custom when the look is designed for this piece.

render_runtime.description: The engine, locked here: remotion, hyperframes or ffmpeg. Present both Remotion and HyperFrames when both are installed and usable for this pipeline.

composition_mode.description: templated assembles the stock scene types into the stock compositions; atelier hand-authors a composition for this piece.

renderer_family.description: The creative grammar for templated work, from the pipeline's list.

name.description: What the deliverable is, for example clip-03-vertical or main-es.

language.description: Language code, such as en or es.

delivery_promise.description: What kind of video is promised. It is checked before rendering, so a still slideshow cannot pass for a motion-led video. The edit carries it unchanged into edit_decisions.

promise_type.description: motion_led: real motion carries the video. source_led: the supplied footage leads. data_explainer: data and charts carry it. teacher_explainer: a step-by-step walk through a concept. screen_demo: software or a website shown working. avatar_presenter: a presenter speaking to camera. hybrid: supplied footage with designed or generated support. localization: an existing video in another language.

motion_required.description: True when the video depends on real motion (video clips, animation), not on camera moves over stills.

source_required.description: True when the operator's supplied footage must lead.

tone_mode.description: Tone of the delivery, such as cinematic, educational, corporate, playful, raw, intimate or epic.

quality_floor.description: The lowest finish the operator accepts.

approved_fallback.description: A lesser form the operator agreed to if the promised one cannot be made: animatic or still_led. null (the default) when none was agreed.

method.description: composition: drawn word by word by the composition from the narration timing. burned: subtitle_gen cues burned in with ffmpeg_caption_burn. files: SRT or VTT files delivered beside the video only. none: no captions.

languages.description: Caption languages, as language codes such as en or es.

tool.description: edge_tts (free, needs the network), piper_tts (free, offline), openai_tts or elevenlabs_tts (paid); supplied for the operator's own recording or the speaker in the footage; none when the video has no narration.

voice_id.description: The voice name or id the tool takes.

rationale.description: Why this voice fits the brief.

delivery_style.description: Plain-language direction, such as warm expert, expressive narrator or crisp tutorial.

pacing_policy.description: How the voice uses pauses, speed and emphasis across the piece.

sample_approval_required.description: True when a voice sample must be approved before the full narration.

music_plan.description: Where the music comes from. Settle it whenever the video has sound.

source_type.description: user_library: a track from the operator's library (music_library). bring_your_own: a track the operator will provide. none: no music.

track_path.description: Path of the chosen track, when known.

notes.description: Where the music plays when not throughout, and anything else the mix must know.

unavailable.description: Needs that a capability without a configured provider would serve, with the alternative offered.

alternative.description: The free or supplied alternative, or the question put to the operator.

paid_step.description: One step that calls a tool which may charge the operator's provider account.

purpose.description: What the step makes and why it is worth paying for.

credit_note.description: The tool's credit note as describe gives it, for example "Uses your OpenAI API credits".

sample_first.description: True when one sample is made and approved before the batch.

quantity.description: How many calls the step makes, the sample included.

free_alternative.description: The free way to cover the same need, and what it changes in the result.

approval.description: The operator's answer at this approval point.

user_notes.description: The operator's answer and any changes asked for, in their words.
